raw_response:
I've been farming these 9 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. My father taught me, and now my son works in a factory over in Handan, but he comes back when I need him for planting and harvest. We have six people in the house, so the farm has to produce, but at least his off-farm wages help us pay for inputs. I'm 70 now—I don't try new things. I do what works, and when I'm not sure, I look at what Old Zhang and the others down the road are doing.

Here is my plan for this year.

**Wheat — 6 mu**

I plant wheat on 6 mu, same as always, around October 10th. I save my own seed most years—why pay the seed station when my wheat grows fine? I put about 12 kg of urea per mu down before planting, plus a little bag of phosphate fertilizer from the village supply shop. Last spring my neighbor tried using less fertilizer to save money, and his wheat turned yellow at jointing. He got poor yield. I'm not making that mistake. When the wheat greens up in March, if it looks a bit pale I topdress another 8 kg of urea per mu. 

I irrigate three times: once after planting if the autumn is dry, once at jointing around Qingming, and once at grain filling. The well has a meter now so water costs more than before, but you cannot skip jointing—that's when the wheat is thirsty. I expect around 400 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

**Maize — 6 mu**

Right after wheat harvest in early June—sometimes only 5 or 6 days later—I plant maize on the same 6 mu. The turnaround is tight. I don't have time for deep tillage, just a quick cultivate and plant. I buy hybrid maize seed, about 2.5 kg per mu, costs me roughly 40 yuan per mu. At planting I put compound fertilizer in the rows, about 15 kg per mu. Then when the plants reach the big trumpet stage in July, I spread another 10 kg of urea per mu. 

I irrigate twice—once right after planting and once at trumpet stage. If August is very dry I might do a third, but usually twice is enough around here. I hire the combine for wheat harvest so I can get the maize seed in the ground fast. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton — 3 mu**

The other 3 mu I plant cotton in late April. My wife is good at picking, and cotton brings money at a good time for winter expenses. I plant about 2 kg of seed per mu. I put down 10 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress once in July with about 5 kg more. I irrigate twice, in June and July. Cotton gets bugs, so I spray 2 or 3 times with whatever the supply store recommends—usually insecticide and a bit of herbicide early on. We pick three or four times from September into October. My daughter-in-law and the grandchildren help after school. It's labor-heavy, but steady. I expect about 240 kg of lint per mu.

**Labor and costs**

Most work is family labor. My wife and I handle the daily jobs. My son comes back for wheat planting, the June rush, and cotton picking. I might hire 3 or 4 days of casual labor for cotton picking if the children are busy. Fertilizer prices have gone up, so I watch every jin, but cutting back costs more in lost yield than it saves. My total spending on seeds, fertilizer, water, pesticide, and a little hired help will be around 3,200 yuan this year.
